### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1acb4f970752aa2ed4cd2c96d6bbacfb7b4776ae` — the merge of head `fa53728a843bc719b9781082da7f958a89c51d75` into base `15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1acb4f970752aa2ed4cd2c96d6bbacfb7b4776ae && git checkout 1acb4f970752aa2ed4cd2c96d6bbacfb7b4776ae
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37 fa53728a843bc719b9781082da7f958a89c51d75 && git checkout -B drift-repro 15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37 && git merge --no-ff fa53728a843bc719b9781082da7f958a89c51d75

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 15764cd723e750c01416cfe91b44bbd0a4c28f37
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fa53728a843bc719b9781082da7f958a89c51d75`
Local-runs: none
Scope: hits: none by path (`reviewFace` over the file list finds no published-schema and no governed path; the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line is what makes the review owed, and the dispatch asked for this tier on a published-type widening) + the whole diff outside the prose face: `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-25031-blocked-unique-apply-limit.test.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-remote-drift-apply-limit.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.blocked-unique-index.integration.test.ts`; `.changeset/25031-blocked-unique-index-apply-limit.md` sentence by sentence; cited code read at the head: `sql-driver.ts` (`applyNullSafeUniquePreflight`, `probeNullSafeUniqueDuplicates`, `applyMigrationEntries`, `applyIndexDriftOp`, `formatDuplicateGroups`), `schema-drift.ts` (`driftFindingWithoutRemedy`), `driver-sql/src/index.ts` export block and `driver-sql/package.json` `exports`, `turso-driver.ts` (`driftApplyLimit`, `applyMigrationEntries`, `applyRemoteIndexDriftOp`, `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS`, the `probeNullSafeUniqueDuplicates` override), `driver-sqlite-wasm/src/sqlite-wasm-driver.ts` (overrides no drift seam), `cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts` (`SqlDriverLike`, `SchemaStack`, `collectDriftApplyLimits`, `describeWithApplyLimits`, `CATEGORY_META`), `cli/src/utils/apply-drop-gates.ts` (`describeDriftEntries`), `cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts` (header, `--json` branch, footer), `cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts` (header contract, the limits read, `notApplied` / PARTIAL / exit), `cli/src/utils/artifact-boot-migration.ts`, `cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.remote-face.integration.test.ts`, `cli/vitest-tiers.ts`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and the "WHICH LEVEL" prose in `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, `docs/adr/0120-…` D4; card #25031 body and comments 6307307994, 6307517392, 6340150456, 6341277431; declaration 6340209215 on #22648; the PR body and its Acceptance notes.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Published surface: `ManagedDriftEntry.applyLimit?: string` (`@objectstack/driver-sql`).** `ManagedDriftEntry` sits in `src/index.ts`'s `export type { … }` block and reaches consumers through `exports["."].types` (`dist/index.d.ts`), so the member is a published widening: one optional key on an exported interface, no existing member changed, no implementer forced to produce it, no reader forced to consume it. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` names the only published change there is. No other exported declaration moves: `SqlDriver.applyNullSafeUniquePreflight` stays `protected` with the same signature; `SqlDriverLike.driftApplyLimit(opType)`, `SchemaStack.driftApplyLimit(entry)` and `TursoDriver.driftApplyLimit(opType)` are byte-identical to `main`. The member's TSDoc states the producer, the absence rule and the "never re-derived from `message`" rule, and each is true of the code. RIGHT.
2. **Producer.** The field is written in exactly one place, `SqlDriver.applyNullSafeUniquePreflight`, inside the duplicates branch (`duplicates.length` above zero) and above the `nullSafeKey ? … : …` message ternary, so both arms (the NULL-safe `recreate_index` tightening and the plain or NULL-safe `create_index`) carry it, a clean probe never does, and nothing else in the repo writes it (`git grep applyLimit` at the head outside tests: one declaration, one assignment, one read). `TursoDriver` inherits it on both faces (its REMOTE face overrides only the probe's statement; `detectTableDrift` is the base's), and `SqliteWasmDriver extends SqlDriver` overriding none of the drift seams. RIGHT; Turso pinned on both faces, sqlite-wasm by construction.
3. **(a) Nothing becomes looser, on any driver.** No guard reads the field. `SqlDriver.applyMigrationEntries` and `TursoDriver.applyMigrationEntries` split on `category` alone, and `category: 'destructive'` on a blocked entry is unchanged by the diff, so a plain apply, dev `autoMigrate: 'safe'` and the artifact boot gate (`artifact-boot-migration.ts` reads `category` only) still never attempt the CREATE. Under `allowDestructive` the apply refuses it as before: the NULL-safe tightening re-probes in `applyIndexDriftOp`'s `recreate_index` arm before any drop; the plain unique CREATE fails on the duplicates and the `create_index` arm reports presence only; on the Turso REMOTE face the failed `write` batch lands in `skipped` through the `catch`. In the CLI the limit is read by `collectDriftApplyLimits` for the human face only: `apply.ts` builds `intended` / `deferred` from `category` and the flag, and `notApplied`, PARTIAL and the exit code never consult `limits` (its comment at the read, verified against the code at :696–:752). The field can only mark an entry as not re-runnable; it admits nothing and skips no guard. RIGHT.
4. **(b) Precedence `entry.applyLimit ?? owner.driftApplyLimit(entry.op.type)`.** Absent (an older or third-party driver, any `SqlDriverLike` without the field, every unblocked entry): `??` falls through and the seam answers exactly as on `main`. Present: the entry is limited; `collectDriftApplyLimits` keeps any non-null string, so even an empty string would tighten, never loosen, and the field's type excludes `null`, so no value exists that silences a transport's per-op limit. Where both would exist they agree ("cannot apply") and only the printed reason differs, the entry's data-dependent one first, which is the more specific of the two; on the one transport with per-op limits (Turso REMOTE) every index op is `'applied'` in `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS`, so no entry today carries both. The owner lookup and its refusal of an undetected entry still run ahead of the read. RIGHT in both directions.
5. **(c) Other surfaces.** The `--json` documents of `plan` (`changes: drift`) and `apply` (`applied`, `skipped`, `notApplied`) emit entries whole, so a blocked entry now carries `applyLimit` there: an additive key, which the changeset states. RIGHT. Rendering, in unchanged code: a limited `create_index` line is `driftFindingWithoutRemedy(d)` followed by `"os migrate apply" cannot apply it on this database: …`; an index op has no remedy suffix to strip, so the entry's full BLOCKED message (duplicate report included) precedes the limit and the duplicate report appears twice on one line, under a group heading that still reads `Destructive (requires --allow-destructive)` (`CATEGORY_META`). Correct behaviour, redundant text: an observation, not a defect of this diff.
6. **(d) The CLI line.** The production diff in `packages/cli` is the one line declaration 6340209215 names (`schema-migrate.ts` :1569) plus the two comment lines above it; no signature moves. RIGHT. The diff also adds `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.blocked-unique-index.integration.test.ts` (278 lines) in the cli lane's package, which the declaration does not name: carried to ③.3.
7. **Tests.** driver-sql pin: plain and organization-scoped blocked entries carry the limit naming the conflicting group, the apply under `allowDestructive` skips them, and two controls (a duplicate-free index has no `applyLimit`, is `safe`, and a plain apply creates it; deduplicating withdraws the limit). Turso: both faces, `driftApplyLimit('create_index')` still `null`, the apply skips. CLI integration: real boot over a SQLite file through `plan`, `apply --yes` and `apply --allow-destructive --yes` (listing with the limits, zero re-run offers, PARTIAL with exit 1 pinned as today's verdict), plus a control pinning the byte-exact unchanged footer and a successful create. The file carries no nightly-tier name, so it is in the queue population (`vitest-tiers.ts`: nightly selects by name only), and `better-sqlite3`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/objectql` are cli devDependencies. The ablation (3 of 4, 2 of 6 and 3 of 4 red with the assignment deleted, every control green) is the dev's reading; not re-run here. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/25031-blocked-unique-index-apply-limit.md`: `@objectstack/driver-sql: patch`, `@objectstack/cli: patch`. Both packages publish (no `private` field; driver-sql carries an `exports` map with `types`). `@objectstack/driver-turso` moves only a test file, so nothing publishes from it and no entry is owed. RIGHT.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset. `none` is right: no authorable key, value or type moves (a driver type and CLI output do). Under maintainer ruling A on #25105 as `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and the "WHICH LEVEL" prose encode it, a declared `none` grades every introduced entry `patch`; `Check Changeset` on this head is `success`. The level is the one the rule prescribes. RIGHT.
- The changeset prose, sentence by sentence against the diff: the `main` behaviour it describes (a block carried in the message only; a seam asking by op type) is `main`'s code at `schema-migrate.ts` :1568; "absent on every other entry": the one assignment sits in the duplicates branch; "On `--json`, a blocked entry now carries this key": entries are emitted whole; "reads the entry's own limit first, then the driver's per-op one": :1569; "listed with the conflicting groups as the reason … the footer and the skip lines stop offering `--allow-destructive` for it … counted among the changes that remain drift": `plan.ts`'s footer branch and `apply.ts`'s `notReRunnable` lines; "A database with no blocked index prints as before": `limits.size === 0` keeps the unchanged branches; "Unchanged: … reports the run PARTIAL with exit 1": `apply.ts` :696–:752. No sentence is false.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Open question 1: should `apply --allow-destructive` stop ending PARTIAL on a declared-limit entry?** Answered: keep it (the dev's option A), and keeping it is in scope to accept. The card's acceptance text ("Wanted") asks for three things: a BLOCKED entry is not offered `--allow-destructive` by `plan`'s footer or `apply`'s skip lines and is listed with its reason and what clears it, in the #23925 / #24958 shape; read from the one place that already says BLOCKED, no second judgement; a database with no blocked entry prints as today. The diff delivers all three; the PARTIAL row in the card's "Measured" table is the consequence of the offer, not a Wanted item. `apply.ts`'s documented contract (#23848 guarantee 4, and the comment at :688) is that a destructive entry the operator confirmed and the driver did not apply makes the run PARTIAL and exit 1 "in both faces", and that `notApplied`, PARTIAL and the exit code never read declared limits (:345); the Turso REMOTE tightening pins the same verdict in `apply.remote-face.integration.test.ts`. With the offer gone, an operator reaches that exit only by forcing `--allow-destructive` against a listing that said the entry cannot be applied, and exit 1 then reports a database that still differs from its metadata, which is true. Option B changes the CLI's exit-code contract for Turso as well and is a `domain:cli` card if anyone wants it; nothing in it blocks this PR.
2. **Open question 2: `Clause-②` and the tier.** The correction from `no` to `yes (widening)` is right (①.1) and `patch` is right (②). On the tier: `reviewFace` over the file list finds no published-schema or governed path, so by the rule the `Clause-②: yes` line alone makes a declaration-face review owed (`TIER_DEFAULT`); the dispatch asked for `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on a published-type widening and this record serves that tier, above the floor and not below it.
3. **Undeclared cross-lane file.** Declaration 6340209215 on #22648 names one line of `schema-migrate.ts`; the PR also lands a 278-line integration test under `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/`. It pins exactly the card's Wanted behaviour and changes no cli production code, so it is no contract matter, but it is a cross-lane write the declaration does not cover. Escalated to the seat: supplement the declaration on #22648 with one line naming the file before the queue holds the PR (the runbook's "cross-package is cross-lane; the PM supplements the seat declaration after the fact").
4. **Acceptance note 1 (the group heading).** True: `renderPlan` groups by `category` and the destructive label reads `Destructive (requires --allow-destructive)`; the entry's own line and the footer say otherwise, and the Turso REMOTE tightening reads the same way today. CLI rendering, outside this card; an observation for the cli lane together with ①.5's doubled duplicate report on the same line.
5. **Acceptance note 2 (`category` unchanged).** True and necessary: it is what keeps every automatic door shut (①.3). Accepted.
6. **Acceptance note 3 (the tightening arm, covered by construction).** True: the assignment is unconditional inside the duplicates branch both arms share, above the arm-specific message. Accepted without a pin.
7. **Acceptance note 4 and out-of-scope finding 2 (the deferred boot flush retries the CREATE and logs `[sql-driver] cannot create unique index …` on every `os migrate apply`).** Pre-existing: `syncDeclaredIndexes` degrades the failure to a log, which is also why the apply's `create_index` arm reports presence only; untouched by this diff and the same on `main`. Not filed by the dev; the seat cards it or dismisses it.
8. **Gates.** Locally NOT MEASURED by the dev: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` (prerequisite: a whole-workspace build), and `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` exited 3 on a shallow clone, then 0 after its fixture commit was fetched. Read on the head at 2026-10-22T13:07:00Z: 25 check-runs `success` (among them `Lint & Repo Gates` and every `Lint ·` job, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, and the claim, branch and single-writer guards), 7 `skipped` (the opt-in and `main`-only batteries), and 7 still `in_progress`: `Test Core (1/6)` through `(6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace`. An in-progress gate is not a pass: this record is the contract verdict alone, and the queue waits for those seven.
9. `dogfood_battery: n/a` is correct (no `!` in the title, no `(narrowing)` arm). `premise_still_valid: true`: the measured `main` rows match the card's. Serial note 6307517392's wake condition held: PR #24893's `d5d814601` and seat 1's PR #25188 `5d66021a7` are both ancestors of the branch point `e5f194b`, and `main` has not moved on the three touched source files since.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-lpzi51`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FaVyM6YvQLg9CsjPVCYc5K`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · `domain:engine` seat 2 (seat post #20966) · `os-bill` · `session_01FaVyM6YvQLg9CsjPVCYc5K` · 2026-10-22T13:10Z · head `fa53728a843bc719b9781082da7f958a89c51d75` · card #25031.

1. **Form:** draft, `Fixes #25031`, assignee `os-bill`, 7 files (+494 / −2). `check-governed-merges --pr 25217`: 0 of 7 paths governed, 496 changed lines ≤ 3000 ⇒ ordinary queue landing, no human-merge tier.
2. **Premise measured:** the dev report 6341277431 measured the blocked unique index on `driver-sql` and both Turso faces, with an ablation that turns every pin red; the contract review read the single producer (`applyNullSafeUniquePreflight`) and the single reader (`SchemaStack.driftApplyLimit`) in code.
3. **Gates:** contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` **PASS** on this head, comment 6341526231 (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` face: `ManagedDriftEntry.applyLimit?: string` is the only published change; no guard reads it, so nothing gets looser on any driver). Check-runs on this head are still running (`Test Core` shards, `Type Check · workspace`). Landing waits for every check green on this head; it is re-read at the flip.
4. **Accepted deviations:**
   - Changeset level `patch` (driver-sql, cli) with `Metadata-protocol: none`: maintainer ruling A on #25105. Confirmed by the review under ②.
   - The dev's open question 1: `apply --allow-destructive` still ends PARTIAL with exit 1 on a blocked unique index. That is `apply.ts`'s documented contract (limits never feed the verdict) and the Turso REMOTE precedent; the card's three "Wanted" items are met as written. Kept (option A). Changing the exit code would be a `domain:cli` contract decision, not this card's.
   - The cli integration test `apply.blocked-unique-index.integration.test.ts` sits outside the one line declared on #22648 (6340209215); the seat supplemented that declaration on #22648. Test only, no cli production code.
5. **Out of scope, disposed:**
   - CLI rendering of a limited `create_index` line repeats the duplicate report (once from the entry's message, once from the limit); the group heading still reads `Destructive (requires --allow-destructive)`; `plan.ts`'s header prose about the `--json` document is now stale. Cosmetic, cli lane, code reading; noted here, not filed.
   - The deferred boot flush retries the blocked CREATE and logs `cannot create unique index …` on each `os migrate apply`: pre-existing, identical on `main`; noted, not filed.
6. **Landing:** once every check on this head is green, the seat flips ready and arms auto-merge through the relay; the card closes on merge by `Fixes #25031`, and the landing comment records the queue branch and `origin/main` readings.
